userStories.title: Add check-test-sleeps scanner core + unit tests
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a pure, unit-testable scanner that detects fixed timed-sleep async waits in test files so that the ban can later be wired as a deterministic check:all gate.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts exists, modeled on scripts/check-debt-markers.ts: a pure scanForSleeps(files: {path,text}[]) function plus a thin import.meta.main CLI; readFileSync (node:fs) is used ONLY inside the import.meta.main entrypoint, so the scanner is unit-testable with injected content. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'export function scanForSleeps' scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts && grep -q 'import.meta.main' scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts]

Detection matches ONLY two anchored forms: (i) Bun.sleepSync(<numeric literal>) as a call, and (ii) new Promise(<id> => setTimeout(<id>, <numeric literal>)). The numeric literal explicitly INCLUDES 0 (a setTimeout(resolve, 0) yield is a match; the sole real 0-literal site is suppressed downstream in US-006, so the scanner keeps no magic-number carve-out). [oracle: bun test]

Detection does NOT match: injected/recorded clocks (sleepFn:, setTimeoutFn =, globalThis.setTimeout =, nowFn:), Bun.sleep( (async), bare callback schedulers setTimeout(cb, n), or variable-interval timers such as setTimeout(resolve, intervalMs). Verified against the known false-positive set (test/dashboard.test.ts:755,789,882-896; test/retry/launcher.test.ts:158-201; test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts:129; test/helpers/wait-for-condition.ts:32; test/helpers/flush-ink.ts:70). [oracle: bun test]

Scope is test/ only: the CLI enumerates test/**/*.{ts,tsx} via new Glob(...).scanSync({ cwd }) with EXCLUDED_DIRS filtered (mirroring check-debt-markers filterScannablePaths); src/ production sleeps are out of scope. [oracle: file-assert grep -q "test/\*\*/\*.{ts,tsx}" scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts]

Suppression is a same-line tracker-ref (CAM-NNN, #N, or an https:// URL), reusing the check-debt-markers CITED_RE convention; NO new inline // cam-ignore comment convention is introduced. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'CITED_RE\|CAM-' scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts]

The CLI prints file:line + a message pointing violators at test/helpers/wait-for-condition.ts to stderr and exits 1 on any un-suppressed violation; it prints an ok line and exits 0 otherwise. [oracle: bun test]

Unit tests (test/check-test-sleeps.test.ts) drive scanForSleeps with injected fixtures covering: a flaggable Bun.sleepSync(<n>) fixture fails; a flaggable promisified setTimeout(<id>,<n>) fixture fails; a setTimeout(resolve, 0) literal fixture fails (0 is matched); a same-line-tracker-ref-suppressed fixture passes; and injected-clock, Bun.sleep-async, bare-scheduler, and variable-interval fixtures all pass. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New file scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts + test/check-test-sleeps.test.ts. Model EXACTLY on scripts/check-debt-markers.ts (pure scan fn + filterScannablePaths + thin CLI, readFileSync only in import.meta.main). Bun.Glob: new Glob('test/**/*.{ts,tsx}').scanSync({ cwd }) returns repo-relative paths (absolute defaults false) per officialDocsConsulted. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard every regex capture group (T | undefined). Anchor the two regex forms tightly so the injected clocks (setTimeoutFn =, globalThis.setTimeout =, sleepFn:, nowFn:) and bare setTimeout(cb, n) schedulers never match (see issue gotchas). Decision (finding #2): the scanner MATCHES the numeric literal 0 with no carve-out; the one real 0-literal yield (flush-ink.ts:22) is handled by tracker-ref suppression in US-006, keeping one uniform escape hatch. Does NOT wire the gate into GATES (that is US-007), so landing this story keeps bun test / check:all green. patterns.md: grep 'sleep\|waitForCondition\|gate' for prior conventions.

userStories.title: Migrate integration sleeps to waitForCondition (group A: tmux-introspect, stop-sidecar-real)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need the fixed Bun.sleepSync waits in the two highest-density integration files replaced by polling their observable condition so that these tests are faster and non-flaky.
acceptanceCriteria: All 13 Bun.sleepSync sites (12 in test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts, 1 in test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts) are replaced by waitForCondition (from test/helpers/wait-for-condition.ts) polling the real observable condition (pane exists / label set / file written / process gone), not a blind fixed poll. [oracle: file-assert test $(grep -c 'Bun.sleepSync(' test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s}') -eq 0]
Any site with genuinely no pollable condition (expected: none in this group) is instead suppressed with a same-line tracker-ref + reason, not left as a bare sleep. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts (12 sites), test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts (1 site). Use waitForCondition(predicate, { timeoutMs, intervalMs }) already on main (CAM-62). For tmux: poll capture-pane / list-panes for the pane/label to exist; for a killed process: poll until the pid/pane is gone; for a file artifact: poll until Bun.file(path).exists(). These are real-I/O integration tests: keep hitting the real tmux/git/fs boundary, just replace 'sleep then assume settled' with 'poll until the condition holds'. Migrations are independent of US-001 (the helper already exists); priority ordering places them after the scanner. patterns.md: grep 'tmux\|integration\|waitForCondition'.
